question: Can one semantic action atomically update an attribute, points, arrow availability, and derived values while every rejected action preserves the complete state?

behaviour_cards.contract: Activate spends the manifest-derived cost and ContextActivate reverses only an allocation made after the source state. Attribute, available points, arrow availability, derived values, and version publish in one state frame.
Unaffordable, stale, rapid-after-exhaustion, and below-source actions return a named error, preserve the complete state byte-for-byte, and do not advance the semantic version.
Use a purpose-built 484x28 title form and restore semantic state and position.

validated_walkthroughs: two Str steps spend exactly four points in two frames
Int step rejects at cost 11 with four points
Agi step and reverse restore source state; a second reverse rejects
third rapid Str step rejects after the second exhausts points
